brief.analysis: Defense has run ahead of the market, but there's no trend confirmation and the short-term average is still climbing. Decisively, the plain reading and the trend-adjusted reading disagree by more than a full move — direct evidence the ratio's average is drifting upward, consistent with a durable rearmament spending shift that post-dates the old 5-year window. The old average is stale, so the apparent stretch is measuring against the wrong benchmark.
brief.report_line: Fade of defense-vs-market: we advise against it — the flat and trend-adjusted signals disagree by more than a full move, direct evidence that structural rearmament has moved the average up and the reversion target is no longer valid.

brief.analysis: Chips have run far ahead of the broad Nasdaq and the move is still going — trend confirmation is weak and the short-term average is still rising, so it hasn't even turned. The AI build-out is a genuine multi-year shift in where earnings accrue, and the implied ~70% round-trip to the old 5-year average treats a structural re-rating as if it were noise; that average is no longer a credible target. The statistics look extreme precisely because the mean itself has moved.
brief.report_line: Fade of chips-vs-Nasdaq: we advise against the full mean-reversion trade — the AI capital-spending cycle has structurally lifted semiconductors' earnings share, so the ~70% snap-back to the old average is a trap, not an edge (regime read is search-limited).

brief.analysis: Gold's run past stocks has already largely reversed — the 200-day-average target is hit and only the 5-year average remains, another ~11% away. The strongest regime argument is that persistent, price-insensitive central-bank gold buying has lifted gold's fair level, so the 5-year average likely sits too low to be a valid finish line; the ratio is not even stretched against its own upward drift, which supports that. Take the reversion that's happened, but don't chase the last leg into a structural buyer.
brief.report_line: Short gold-vs-stocks: the quick snap-back is booked, but we size down because sustained central-bank gold buying may have permanently raised the target, making the last ~11% to the old average a fight against a structural bid (regime read is search-limited).

brief.analysis: Miners have run ahead of the market and are beginning to roll over — decent confirmation, short-term average turned, 200-day-average target hit. The catch is that mining is riding the same precious- and industrial-metals strength that is lifting gold and silver, so a chunk of the move may be structural rather than a dislocation, and the historical evidence here is thin (only two prior episodes). Trade the pullback that's underway, but keep it small until the metals complex cools.
brief.report_line: Short miners-vs-market: the near-term reversion is real and partly booked, but we size down because the move is tied to a broad metals-complex strength that may be structural, on a thin two-episode track record (regime read is search-limited).

brief.analysis: Silver spiked violently ahead of gold and is already rolling over — full trend confirmation, the short-term average has turned down, and the 200-day-average target is achieved. Silver-versus-gold is one of the most reliably mean-reverting relationships in metals; sharp silver over-runs historically fade, and the ratio shows no sign its underlying average has drifted. This is the cleanest rubber-band snap in the book.
brief.report_line: Short silver-vs-gold: a clean, well-confirmed reversion of a classic violent silver over-run, with regime risk low and the historical average intact as a valid target.
